findings.text: A sequential reporting interface enumerates recorded dependency chains. The initial position yields a header token, negative positions are rejected, and later positions map to successive stored chains through a helper that locates the next valid index. Termination performs no action, and an operations table wires the four callbacks together.

Chain display separates a global header from individual records. The header flags exhaustion when the free pool is empty. Each record reports its interrupt context with one of four labels and then lists only levels whose class carries a key, pairing a key pointer with a readable name followed by separation.

An aggregate status reporter summarizes validator activity into grouped tallies for safe against unsafe usage across generic and soft and hard interrupt settings, including read variants, alongside totals for classes, dependencies, chains, stack usage and reuse. A debug extension under a build option adds lookup, cycle, redundancy and interrupt transition event counters.

Only classes flagged in use contribute to counts. Absence of usage bits denotes unused, presence of solely the generic used bit denotes uncategorized. Forward totals accumulate per-class values, overall direct totals combine cross products of unsafe and safe populations with known edges, and the combined maximum multiplies incremented per-context chain counts.

Per-class snapshot storage couples a class reference with a copy of its counters. A collection provides a fixed capacity table sized by the maximum key limit together with an end marker delimiting the populated prefix used for traversal and ordering.

Per-class reporting moves through capture, traversal, optional clearing and release. Capture snapshots active classes and orders them, traversal first emits a header then one record per snapshot, an input starting with zero clears statistics for all active classes while other inputs preserve state, and release discards the snapshot buffer. Sequential and file callbacks wire the lifecycle together.

Snapshot order ranks larger total wait operations first, summing both directions. Durations appear rounded and scaled for display with fixed fractional precision. Directional sections appear only with corresponding hold activity, bounce tallies accompany wait and hold summaries, two address detail groups cease at the first empty slot, separator rows frame the header and detail groups, and the header cautions when global debugging is disabled.

Observation of a class display name and identity occurs inside a scheduler read-side critical section, with release before formatting. Absence of both values skips the record, while absence of only the name falls back to a key-derived label with version and subclass suffixes appended when present.

Startup registration exposes diagnostic files for chain enumeration, aggregate counters and per-class detail, using read-only access except for the per-class file which permits owner writes to trigger clearing. Availability of some files depends on proving and statistics build options.
Maximum supported nested torture depth is eight.
Per-class detail report identifies its layout as version zero point four.
Diagnostic names are lockdep plus lockdep_chains plus lockdep_stats plus lock_stat.

Torture abstraction groups lifecycle hooks with nested and single acquisition and release for exclusive access, acquisition and release for shared access, delay injection for each direction, a priority adjustment hook, storage for saved interrupt state, and a descriptive label.

Execution context records realized exclusive and shared thread counts, debugging and initialization indicators, an atomic error tally, a pointer to the active abstraction, and separate statistic tables for each role counting failures and successes. A deferred callback node pairs a header with a stop flag, tracked through a global list head.

Global state holds a statistics thread handle, dynamically sized tables for exclusive and shared workers, a boolean exclusive-held marker, an atomic shared-held count, and a timestamp of the latest release.

Default selection favors a realtime-safe spin variant when realtime preemption is enabled and the ordinary spin variant otherwise. Optional processor bindings for both worker roles reside in dynamically allocated masks with explanatory comments.

Binding update allocates a mask on demand, parses a processor list, and upon allocation or parse failure emits a warning and reverts to all processors. Retrieval renders the current set, emptiness requires both availability and nonemptiness, and both directions are exposed through paired callbacks.

Priority control remains idle unless a selector enables boosting. Otherwise ordinary workers gain elevated scheduling at randomized intervals scaled by exclusive worker count and a factor, remain elevated for a longer randomized duration, then return to normal, with an unconditional restoration path when no random state is supplied.
A testing-only abstraction reports success while performing no exclusion, leaving shared state unprotected. Its use is confined to baseline measurements and must never guard real data.

Stress synchronization relies on a single global spin primitive. One path acquires and releases with interrupts unchanged, while another preserves the prior interrupt state inside the active abstraction for restoration after the critical region.

Hold-time emulation mixes infrequent extended waits scaled by a configured duration, frequent brief pauses, and sporadic voluntary yields, with occurrence rates normalized by the realized exclusive worker population to sustain contention. Extended waits report elapsed ticks.
Diagnostic prefixing for this module is transparent, forwarding the supplied message format without added decoration.
Startup values for the execution context indicate no realized workers, cleared debugging and initialization markers, zero recorded errors, and null abstraction and statistic references.
